question: Suppose $S$ is a set with $n \geq 2$ elements, and $f: S \to S$ is an injective but not surjective function. Is this possible? Write Yes/No and a one-line reason.
explanation: No. For finite set $S$, if $f$ is injective, it must also be surjective, so such a function cannot exist.

options.A: Yes, every injective function on a finite set is not surjective
options.C: No, for a finite set $S$, every injective function $f:S\to S$ is also surjective
options.D: No, because no function from $S$ to $S$ can be injective
